task: Step 5 corrected event-sequence CTC baseline on the expanded S22 data
representation: official_v1_event_sequence: ordered (25,306) event tensors concatenated to (25U,306)

reporting_framework.primary_metric: character_f1 (aligned-character precision/recall harmonic mean), under evaluation_error_decomposition
reporting_framework.primary_metric_reason: CER and recall are length-sensitive in opposite directions. Within the real-label condition alone, held-out CER moves substantially with the decoded length ratio while character F1 stays essentially flat, so CER conflates which characters are recovered with how aggressively the decoder emits or withholds them.
reporting_framework.secondary_metrics: S/D/I rates per target character and the decoded-length ratio
reporting_framework.control: target permutation, a no-valid-signal-assignment control, not a competing decoder
reporting_framework.cer: reported for continuity with earlier phases, explicitly interpreted as sensitive to output length

primary_split_reason: C is sentence-disjoint and spans both sessions: train on both list1 blocks, evaluate on both list2 blocks.
splits_excluded_reason: F and G are CROSS-SESSION WITH SENTENCE OVERLAP and cannot support a generalization claim.

evaluation_error_decomposition.definition: CER = (S + D + I) / N, N = target characters; counts pooled over all seeds
evaluation_error_decomposition.length_robust_note: CER and hit recall are both length-sensitive in opposite directions: a shorter hypothesis caps its insertions and so lowers CER, while a longer hypothesis gets more chances to align a character and so raises recall. character_f1 is the harmonic mean of aligned-character precision and recall and is the length-robust comparison.

unrelated_sentence_reference.what_it_is: each held-out sentence scored against the length-matched training sentence; no model involved
